body.name: Dual-slope multiscale rounding algorithm
body.construction: Given rational \(F\) and an optimal rational table \(q^\star=N\pi^\star\), aggregate repeated atoms and form the optimal-support slope intervals \(I_{as}\).  For arms \(1,2\), use the root interval \([-1/2,5/4]\), and for arm \(3\), use \([-3/2,0]\).  At depth \(\ell\), divide each arm-specific root into \(D_\ell=2^\ell\) consecutive cells of width \(h_{1,\ell}=h_{2,\ell}=(7/4)2^{-\ell}\) and \(h_{3,\ell}=(3/2)2^{-\ell}\), taking every cell left-closed and right-open except that the last cell is right-closed.  Form \(\mathcal P_{a,\ell}\) by grouping the atom intervals contained in a common cell and declaring every interval not contained in one cell to be a singleton.  From fine to coarse depth, replace the residual table on its current support by a rational basic feasible table with the current integer cluster margins, freeze the integer parts of its cells, and pass the remaining mass upward.  Match the selected and required atoms independently along each partition tree and apply the three resulting bijections to the selected rows.  Output the resulting \(T_{\mathrm{alg}}\in\mathcal S_N(F)\).
